subject: Reflective latents & Composite variables not working

messages.author: eba58fc18ddb028e
messages.subject: Reflective latents & Composite variables not working
parts:
Hello everyone :)
I`ve been trying to fit my theoretical model in lavaan and it doesn`t seem to work at all. I am using runMI as I have missing data & WLSMV estimator for robust results with ordinal variables. Based on theory we have  3 composite variables and 1 reflective latent to which all the composites regress.
As you can see I tried to fix the error variances of composite variables (governance, actors & resource) to zero, which would turn them to composites. Sooo this gives me many errors basically saying that the solution is not found. I have tried doing different composite variable options such as changing =~ to <~ and changing the syntax to governance =~ 0 and regressing all the observed variables to the composite but these don`t seem to work either.

Here`s my model:
model.5 <- '
# measurement model
    eco_outcomes =~ all_sp_box + all_m2_box + all_no_box + qlty_avg_all + eco_box_avg + weeds_all_avg
      governance =~ s2_group_meetings + s2_involvement_rc + s2_organization_rc
          actors =~ gsize_rc + s2_stability + s2_others_location + relatedness_rc
                     + s1_worries_rc + s2_damage_previous + s2_social_capital + start_year_rc
        resource =~ box_avg_rc + effort_all + s1_more_box + shade_avg_all + privacy_avg_all
#regressions
eco_outcomes ~ actors + governance + resource
actors ~ governance
#residual correlations?
governance ~~ 0*governance
actors ~~ 0*actors
resource ~~ 0*resource
'

#fit the model5
fit.model5 <- sem.mi(model.5, gb.sem1, m=20, miPackage="mice", 
                     seed=12345, estimator = "WLSMV", ordered = c("s2_damage_previous", "shade_avg_all", "privacy_avg_all",
                                                              "s2_involvement_rc", "s1_more_box",
                                                              "s2_stability", "s2_group_meetings", "s2_organization_rc"))
summary(fit.model5, standardized = T, fit.measures = TRUE)
fitmeasures(fit.model5, pool.robust = TRUE)

My question is: Do you have any advice how I can build composite variable sem in lavaan / does this have any chance of working? I also tried csem but I think runMI doesn`t support it

Thank you in advance,
Laura

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Reflective latents & Composite variables not working
parts:
Laura--
     Your syntax would not create composites. Your syntax line:
eco_outcomes ~ actors + governance + resource

says that actors, governance and resource predict the (previously defined) common factor (using the =~ operator) eco_outcomes.

Your later lines:

governance ~~ 0*governance
actors ~~ 0*actors
resource ~~ 0*resource

declare that common factors (again, via the =~ operator) governance, actors and resource have zero variance. These variables are not dependent on anything, so this is 0 TOTAL variance. Your previous syntax defines these variables as common factors, which cannot have 0 total variance.

You could define eco_outcomes to have 0 residual variance:

eco_outcomes ~~ 0*eco_outcomes

meaning that the three predictors perfectly predict the outcome. This might well be in conflict with the prior common factor specification of eco-outcomes, and you will see the impact in terms of lack of fit.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Reflective latents & Composite variables not working
parts:
The =~ operators that you use create common factors, not composites. Your model as drawn will be not statistically identified, if estimated within a common factor framework. A package like cSEM will estimate models where variables are specified as composites (in a sense--my thinking is a good bit confused right now, and it would take an essay to explain). cSEM uses lavaan syntax, including interpreting lavaan's wonky <~ "formative measurement" operator.
--Ed Rigdon

Laura,

Your question that I was responding to was:
"You mean that I can`t have 0 total variance for these "composite variables"? "

You specified total, not error (better called "disturbance").
Disturbance variances can usually be set to zero, though it may have
consequences for estimation.

Pat

>> There is no such thing as a variable--formative or reflective--with
>> zero total variance. By definition, it's a constant.
>>
>> On Wed, Oct 28, 2020 at 9:37 AM Laura Tuominen <laura.s....@utu.fi> wrote:
>> >
>> > Hei,
>> >
>> > Thank you for a quick answer!
>> > You mean that I can`t have 0 total variance for these "composite variables"?
>> > I removed the
>> > governance ~~ 0*governance

>> >> Laura--
>> >> Your syntax would not create composites. Your syntax line:

>> >> eco_outcomes ~ actors + governance + resource
>> >>

>> >>

>> >>

>> >> actors ~~ 0*actors
>> >> resource ~~ 0*resource

>> >>
>> >> You could define eco_outcomes to have 0 residual variance:
>> >>
>> >> eco_outcomes ~~ 0*eco_outcomes
>> >>
>> >> meaning that the three predictors perfectly predict the outcome. This might well be in conflict with the prior common factor specification of eco-outcomes, and you will see the impact in terms of lack of fit.

parts:
Hi Pat,

Thank you for the answer, you are right. So what I was confused about is why total variance is 0, if I set the disturbance variance of composites to 0 and then set the composites to predict the reflective latent?

Thank you,
Laura

torstai 5. marraskuuta 2020 klo 18.12.11 UTC+2 mal...@malonequantitative.com kirjoitti:
Laura,

Your question that I was responding to was:

"You mean that I can`t have 0 total variance for these "composite variables"? "

You specified total, not error (better called "disturbance").
Disturbance variances can usually be set to zero, though it may have
consequences for estimation.

Pat
